reason: 'Volumineux' (bulky, large in volume) said of the perianth, the underground parts, the crown and the inflorescence matches PATO's increased volume. This follows the earlier rules for 'enlarged' and 'tall'.
A hyphenated pair of two shape values is a shape between them, handled like 'linear-lanceolate'. Both values already exist in PATO.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: oblanceolate PATO_0002330 – oblong PATO_0000946; 'narrowly' kept as a modifier)
reason: This is a continuum between two existing shapes plus the degree word 'narrowly'. It does not need a term of its own.

label: hyalodermous
definition: A structural quality inhering in a stem by virtue of the stem's outermost cortical cells forming a hyalodermis: a layer of enlarged, thin-walled, empty and hyaline cells.
reason: A bryological stem character (a layer of clear outer cells, as in Sphagnum and some pleurocarps) with no term in PO or PATO. PATO_0000964 transparent would leave out that these cells form a distinct layer. NOTE: Botany-specific (bryophytes).
A misspelling of 'pedunculate'. 'Short-' and 'long-pedunculate' keep the length as a modifier.
The word has mixed senses: a partly opened flower, a moderately sparse crown ('cime demi-claire'), and a loose inflorescence. A degree of openness is not a fixed value.
Lanulose means finely or shortly woolly, a lesser form of lanate (synonym: woolly). At 10 statements a separate small-scale class like puberulous is not justified.

target: new: coloured marking (blotchy PATO_0000329 + colour of the blotches purple PATO_0000951)
reason: This combines a pattern quality with the colour of the marks, not the colour of the whole part. A single colour term would misstate the part as purple.
A vinelike stem or plant grows up on supports or trails like a vine, which is the climbing growth habit.
A plain negation of the existing FLOPO value 'beaked' for fruits and cypselae.

target: new: conjunction of two values (spirally arranged FLOPO:0991114 and imbricate FLOPO:0991063)
reason: Two existing values hold at once: glumes or perigynia set along a spiral and overlapping. Annotate both on the same part.

target: new: conjunction of two values (ciliated PATO_0001408 and spiny PATO_0001365)
reason: The margin is fringed with stiff, spine-like cilia. Both parts of the word are existing values already used for flora margins.
Uncoloured glands, florets and glume margins ('non colorés') lack colour, which is PATO's colorless.
Conchiform means shaped like a shell, which is exactly PATO_0040007.
Ramose (Latin 'ramosus') means branched. PATO lists ramified as a synonym of branched.
'Broadly' adds nothing to a shape that is already round. Keep it as a degree modifier on orbicular.

target: new: conjunction of two values (undulate PATO_0000967 and scalloped PATO_0001889, synonym crenate)
reason: A margin that is both wavy and set with rounded teeth. Two existing values hold together, not a continuum between them.
Geocarpic fruits ripen below the ground surface after being pushed into the soil. On a fruit this is the existing subterranean value, and 'not geocarpic' becomes its negation.
The senses differ by bearer: radial symmetry of corolla lobes, radial rows of fibre and palisade cells, synangia like spokes. No single quality fits, and the anatomical bearers have no PO class here.
'Crown' here is an unnamed generic part: a persistent calyx crown on fruits, or a ring of spinules on prickles. Its absence cannot be stated without knowing which part it is.
This negates the existing value adherent. The other part named (testa, exostome) goes in the 'towards' slot of docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.
Eporose moss leaf-cell walls have no pores. PO has no pore class to state an absence, so negate PATO perforate.
'Sans limbe' on leaves, sheaths and cataphylls means bladeless, as in the earlier rule for 'bladeless'. The calyx case ('without limb') is a different part and should not take this rule.
In botany 'oval' is broadly elliptic, and 'short-' only makes it broader. This follows the earlier mapping of 'broadly oval' to elliptic, not PATO's loose synonym oval under ovate.
French 'sacciforme' means sac-shaped, which is the existing value saccate.
'Trièdre' or 'triédrique' seeds and fruits are three-sided. This follows the rule for 'triquetrous'.
The acumen is the drawn-out tip of the apex, so the measurement is the length of the leaf apex. The bracteole examples need their own organ's apex.
'Diminished florets' in grass spikelets are reduced, smaller florets. Midribs 'diminished toward the apex' are a gradient better left to the stage/position context.
Even-sized leaves or glands are parts of one kind that are the same size, which is exactly the FLOPO value equal.
Limp, floating leaves bend without stiffness. PATO has no flaccid term, and flexible is the nearest existing quality, the opposite of the 'rigid' rule (inflexible).
